titles.title: Tar Sands Tax Loophole Elimination Act
Tar Sands Tax Loophole Elimination Act
A bill to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to clarify that products derived from tar sands are crude oil for purposes of the Federal excise tax on petroleum, and for other purposes.

action.text: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.

bill.summary:
Tar Sands Tax Loophole Elimination Act
This bill expands the definition of crude oil for purposes of the federal excise tax on crude oil received at a U.S. refinery and imported petroleum to include bitumen or bituminous mixtures or oil derived from such mixtures (including tar sands) and oil derived from kerogen-bearing sources (including oil shale). As background, a federal excise tax is imposed on crude oil received at a U.S. refinery and imported petroleum in the amount of $0.26 per barrel (in 2025). The excise tax funds (1) the Hazardous Substance Superfund Trust Fund, which finances the remediation of certain environmentally contaminated sites; and (2) through 2025, the Oil Spill Liability Trust Fund, which finances certain costs associated with the cleanup of oil spills.
